title: Consequence Event
description: ONE normalized 'action + reviewed consequence' event. Every acting surface (perception pipes, cabinet officers, crew subagents) emits this same shape, so proposal rates, outcome quality, and review verdicts are queryable across the whole estate with one query. Graduation math reads ONLY this ledger. See docs/consequence-ledger.md for source mappings and adoption.

ts.description: When the action happened (ISO 8601, UTC preferred).

kind.description: Which estate acted: a perception pipe, a cabinet officer, or a crew subagent.

id.description: Stable actor identifier — pipe name (e.g. 'commitment-ledger'), officer slug (e.g. 'cos'), or crew agent id.

lane.description: Lane / context slug the action belongs to (matches instance/config/contexts/<slug>.yml). null when the action is estate-wide.

action.description: What was done, verb-first kebab/snake form (e.g. 'drafted-reply', 'auto-closed-commitment', 'claimed-task', 'deployed-preview').

action_type.description: [FIX-1] First-class action-type enum — the (lane × action_type) cell key the authority-matrix gate reads and graduation math keys on. Stamped at emit time by the SAME shared classify_action() the gate uses (framework/authority/classifier.py), so the ledger and the verdict table can never disagree about what an action is. Optional/nullable: absent when not yet stamped (the unmeasured default). The CLOSED branch MUST mirror classifier.ACTION_TYPES exactly (CI-asserted) — do not drift that list from the classifier. THE OPEN BRANCH (2026-07-29) accepts a NAMESPACED id (<namespace>/<operation>): an operation this deployment declared and bound to a framework risk class. Namespacing is what keeps the two vocabularies un-collidable, so a declaration can never redefine a closed member. Without the open branch the ledger could key no cell on any operation the shipped vocabulary does not name, and such an operation could be neither graduated nor demoted on evidence — the ladder would be unreachable for the whole of that operator's work.

subject.description: Who/what the action concerned — a person handle, thread id, board item, commit, outcome node.

decision_verdict.description: [T3] The F4 scorer's tone-blind DECISION verdict for this case (scorer._DEC keys). Optional/nullable — absent for non-eval acting surfaces and legacy rows. Descriptive on the row; the bar keys on review.verdict, not this.

intent_verdict.description: [T3] The F4 scorer's INTENT-alignment verdict (scorer.judge_with_oauth). Optional/nullable. '' / 'error' = the intent layer did not run (decision-only path). review.verdict is mapped FROM this at emit time (aligned->confirmed, divergent->wrong, partial/error/''->unknown) so an intent-based review_confirmed_rate becomes measurable.

intent_composite.description: [T3] The F4 scorer's decision-dominant, intent-penalizing composite (scorer.composite), 0.0–1.0. Optional/nullable — absent when no intent layer ran.

endorsement.description: [T3] The case's endorsement label (Case.endorsement: unknown | regretted | constrained | corrected | ...). Non-empty string when present; nullable/absent when unlabeled. Kept a loose string (not a frozen enum) because the endorsement vocabulary is still being wired (design F4).

refs.description: Links/ids grounding the event: message ids, board item ids, PR URLs, vault note paths, org_events event_id.

proposal.description: The approval-gate half. Absent or required:false for actions below the proposal bar (pure reads, reflex bookkeeping).

required.description: Whether this action class gates on human approval (propose-first posture or hard ceiling).

decision.description: The human's decision at the gate. null = still pending (or not required). 'edited' = approved with changes — counts as a correction for graduation math.

decided_at.description: When the decision landed. null while pending.

outcome.description: What actually happened after the action executed.

status.description: 'ok' = executed and held; 'failed' = executed and broke/bounced/was reverted; 'unknown' = not yet resolvable.

evidence.description: Pointer or short note proving the status — test run, deploy id, sent-message ref, resolver note. null when status is 'unknown'.

review.description: The reviewed half — filled later by the reasoning-review / architect loop comparing expectation to reality.

verdict.description: 'confirmed' = the action's expectation matched reality; 'wrong' = it did not (lesson material); 'unknown' = reviewer could not determine.

lesson_ref.description: Pointer to the written lesson when verdict is 'wrong' (e.g. a lessons file anchor). null otherwise.

sim.description: [SIE-7] Quarantine marker. Present-and-true ONLY on events emitted under CABINET_SIM_MODE=1 (replay simulations). Enforced to agree with the target dir at the single write chokepoint: a sim:true row can land ONLY in a '-sim' event dir and a non-sim row NEVER lands there, so simulated consequences can never contaminate live graduation/breaker/cell math. read_ledger drops sim rows for live consumers. Absent on all live rows (never written as false).
